intended_object: The canonical isomorphism (Sym^n_R M)|_X ≅ Sym^n_{R|_X}(M|_X): restricting the n-th symmetric power of a sheaf of modules M over a sheaf of commutative rings R to the slice site C/X gives the symmetric power of the restriction. Inferred from the docstring and the name.
explanation: The body applies the library's general `pushforwardSymmetricPowerIso` to `Over.forget X` with the topology `J.over X`. Restricting to the slice site C/X is exactly this pushforward. The general isomorphism is built from three canonical pieces: the description of the sheaf symmetric power as the sheafification of the sectionwise symmetric power, the comparison saying that pushforward commutes with sheafification, and the sectionwise isomorphism, which is the identity on sections. The result is therefore the intended canonical isomorphism, and it is natural in M. The setting (a sheaf of commutative rings on an arbitrary site, an arbitrary object X) is the natural one. The extra instance hypotheses on `J.over X` only ensure that sheafification exists on the slice site. Mathlib has no symmetric powers of sheaves of modules, so there is no more general counterpart.
